title: Local Ricci-pinching maxima on an almost-abelian group
actual: Read the full original six searchable PDF pages as text and rendered pixels, and the full hash-bound source TeX.
proof: For a fixed five-dimensional simply connected group with bracket A_u = J ⊕ uE12 and 0<u<1/2, the standard metric is a nonstrict local maximum of F=Scal²/‖Ric‖², with value 1/3. A metric on the same group has value 9/17. The standard metric is a Ricci soliton on the isometric product Euclidean 2-space × Heisenberg 3-space, but its Ricci operator cannot have the required derivation decomposition for the specified group.

The Schur complement and basis change give cT⁻¹A_uT for every nearby inner product, including arbitrary cross terms. The invariant generalized zero eigenspace and smooth orthonormal frame preserve the unrestricted lower-left block, while the quotient has trace zero and determinant one. Scale and orthogonal conjugation preserve F.

The full orthogonal slice gives P=q−8s²=Q+R. For v in a compact interval inside (0,1/2), Q is bounded below by c₀ρ² and the remainder is bounded by 50ρ³. Zero transverse directions belong to the exact constant-value family, so the degenerate Hessian does not require a strict-maximum argument.

The Ricci derivation test uses both rotation brackets and the nonzero shear bracket. Direct conjugation gives the competitor and the semidirect metric splits explicitly as the product. The flat endpoint u=0 makes the ratio undefined; at u=1/2 a shear produces P=−t⁴ and exceeds 1/3. No assertion about arbitrary groups, real type, or cross-group optimization.
